narrative: 童年、悲恸、一个吞噬讲述者的故事：手和纸张贴近镜头，装订线的另一侧是一个世界。文字应该是不可辨读的纹理，这样字母就不会显得混乱失真。
一个世界正在溢出。一个没有传送门的图书馆广角镜头，就只是一间图书馆。
当没有任何东西离开书页时，它就是错误的工具；如果你想要的是一座没有书的城堡，也是错误的用法。童话城堡（Fairytale Castle）才是那个目的地。
how: 足够近，让书本占据画面近三分之一，24mm到50mm焦段，固定机位或朝着装订线做一次极轻微的推进。主光来自书页本身（光或天气从纸张中溢出），再配一盏昏暗的房间灯。
保持文字作为一种纹理。Prompt: Lost-in-a-book of [Subject], a reader falling into illustration, pages becoming rooms.
when: 一个孩子或成人站在故事的门槛上，悲恸打开了一页书，一则吞噬讲述者的故事。不要把它当作沙发上合上书本的阅读静帧来用。
vs: 物体传送门（Object Portal）是通过任意物体实现的通用装置。书中奇遇则明确指定这本书就是那扇门。
童话城堡是那扇门另一侧的世界。要展现出装订线上的那道合页，否则你拥有的只是一间图书馆。
examples_film: 《大魔域》（The NeverEnding Story）把书变成一道你可以坠入其中的门槛。《墨水心》（Inkheart）把阅读当作一扇带有后果的门。
静帧应该在近景有纸张，并有一个世界正从装订线中溢出。
mistakes: 一个人坐在沙发上看书，或一座没有书页的城堡。破绽是没有门槛感。
修正方法：近景有一本翻开的书，有东西正从装订线中溢出，读者正望向书中或正坠入其中。

faq.q: 电影中的书中奇遇（Lost in a Book）是什么？
faq.a: 一种传送门配方：近景中一本翻开的书，书页变成了房间，读者站在那道合页上。书在这里是一扇门，而不是一件道具。

faq.q: 书中奇遇（Lost in a Book）与物体传送门（Object Portal）的区别
faq.a: 物体传送门是任意物体充当门。书中奇遇则明确指定了纸张、装订线，以及溢出的插画。如果那扇门是一个衣柜或一块屏幕，你想要的是它那个更通用的近亲。

faq.q: 什么时候该用书中奇遇？
faq.a: 童年、悲恸、一个吞噬讲述者的故事。跳过没有传送门的图书馆广角镜头。

faq.q: 如何为AI图像或视频撰写书中奇遇的提示词？
faq.a: 先写前景中翻开的书，然后保持文字不可辨读，展现出那道合页。

narrative: Childhood, grief, a story that eats the teller: hands and paper close to lens, a world on the other side of the binding. Type should be unreadable texture so letters do not garble.
One world spills. A library wide with no portal is just a library.
It is the wrong tool when nothing leaves the page, and the wrong tool if you wanted a castle without a book. Fairytale castle is the destination.
how: Close enough that the book occupies the near third, 24mm to 50mm, lock-off or a tiny push into the gutter. Key from the page (light or weather leaving the paper) plus a dim room lamp.
Keep type as texture. Prompt: Lost-in-a-book of [Subject], a reader falling into illustration, pages becoming rooms.
when: A child or adult at the threshold of a story, grief that opens a page, a tale that eats the teller. Do not use it as a couch-reading still with a closed book.
vs: Object Portal is the generic device through any object. Lost in a book names the volume as the door.
Fairytale Castle is the world on the other side. Show the hinge in the binding or you only had a library.
examples_film: The NeverEnding Story makes the book a threshold you can fall through. Inkheart treats reading as a door with consequences.
The still should have paper in the near plane and a world leaving the gutter.
mistakes: A person reading on a couch, or a castle with no page. The tell is no threshold.
Fix it: open book in the near plane, something leaving the gutter, reader looking in or falling in.

faq.q: What is Lost in a Book in film?
faq.a: A portal recipe: an open book in the near plane, pages becoming rooms, a reader at the hinge. The book is a door, not a prop.

faq.q: Lost in a Book vs Object Portal
faq.a: Object portal is any object as a door. Lost in a book specifies paper, gutter, illustration spilling. If the door is a wardrobe or a screen, you wanted the generic cousin.

faq.q: When should I use Lost in a Book?
faq.a: Childhood, grief, a story that eats the teller. Skip library wides with no portal.

faq.q: How do I prompt Lost in a Book for AI image or video?
faq.a: Open book in foreground, then: Lost-in-a-book of [Subject], a reader falling into illustration, pages becoming rooms. Keep type unreadable. Show the hinge.
